ai.description: *Hylarana leptoglossa* is a slender frog reaching 5–7 cm. It is brown or olive with a distinct pale dorsolateral fold and a dark mask. It features long, slender toes and a pointed snout.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Hylarana leptoglossa* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous white or cream-colored dorsolateral fold that extends clearly from behind the eye.
ai.habitat: Cope's Assam Frog inhabits moist evergreen and semi-evergreen forests, typically found near streams and pools at elevations ranging from 200 to 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: Cope’s Assam Frog is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small invertebrates along the damp forest floors and stream banks of its habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hylarana leptoglossa* breeds during the monsoon, laying large clutches of small, pigmented eggs in stagnant or slow-moving water bodies.
ai.distributionRemarks: Cope's Assam Frog inhabits Northeast India, specifically Assam and Mizoram, typically found in hilly regions at elevations between 200 and 1,200 meters.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Hylarana leptoglossa* consists of a series of short, pulsed, high-pitched chirps typically emitted from near streams in forested habitats.
